criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then every tab is reachable and every card drills down one level.
Given sample mode, when any tab is shown, then the sample data is visibly labelled as sample.

Given the Command Center, when any tab renders, then .colaberry/plan.json and .colaberry/progress.json are both committed in this repo and every tab reads its content from them at runtime rather than from hard-coded values.
Given the Command Center, when any tab is shown, then .colaberry/manifest.json is committed in this repo and every tab shows how old that data is and warns when the age exceeds a week.
Trust — no tab shows a number, a connection or a result the project has not actually produced.
Given a valid SQL Server connection string, when I connect to the database, then I should be able to execute a basic SQL query.
Given an invalid SQL Server connection string, when I attempt to connect, then I should receive an error message indicating the connection failure.
Trust: Every query execution must be logged with the user ID and timestamp.

stories.notes: Verified end-to-end against a real local SQL Server 2025 instance (commit 401383d): both Windows Integrated and SQL Authentication, and Encrypt=yes enforcement. Unit tests mock pyodbc; the real-server pass confirmed both auth modes and the invalid-connection failure path.

outstanding: Given a valid SQL Server connection string, when I connect to the database, then I should be able to execute a basic SQL query.
Given an invalid SQL Server connection string, when I attempt to connect, then I should receive an error message indicating the connection failure.
Trust: Every query execution must be logged with the user ID and timestamp.

criteria.text: Given a CSV file, when I upload it, then the system should detect columns and datatypes.
Given a CSV file with duplicates, when I upload it, then the system should identify duplicate records.
Trust: All uploads are logged with user details and file metadata.

stories.notes: Uses Python's stdlib csv module, not Apache Commons CSV as the brief named (Java-only, incompatible with this Python repo) — confirmed with the user. Only tested against synthetic fixtures, not messy real-world CSVs (quoted commas, BOM, mixed line endings).

outstanding: Given a CSV file, when I upload it, then the system should detect columns and datatypes.
Given a CSV file with duplicates, when I upload it, then the system should identify duplicate records.
Trust: All uploads are logged with user details and file metadata.

stories.notes: Uses a lightweight keyword-based intent parser, not BERT as the brief named — confirmed with the user (heavy dependency mismatch for a walking skeleton). 5-intent taxonomy is a toy list with no grounding in real user questions yet.

outstanding: Given a natural language question, when I ask it, then the system should interpret it correctly.
Given an ambiguous question, when I ask it, then the system should suggest potential interpretations.

criteria.text: Given a previous question, when I ask a follow-up, then the system should remember the context.
Given a new session, when I ask a follow-up, then the system should prompt for context.
Trust: All follow-up interactions are logged with user details.

stories.notes: In-memory session store only (no persistence layer exists in this repo yet); no background expiry, checked lazily on next follow-up. Reuses STORY-003's interpret_question() for ambiguity detection rather than a second parser. 'Remembers context' means returning raw question history only — nothing yet resolves a follow-up against that history.

outstanding: Given a previous question, when I ask a follow-up, then the system should remember the context.

criteria.text: Given a user question, when the system interprets it, then it should suggest at least one potential interpretation.
Given an ambiguous question, when the system interprets it, then it should suggest multiple interpretations for user selection.
Trust: Every interpretation suggestion must be logged with the question and user ID.

stories.notes: REQ-004's acceptance criteria and failure paths (ambiguous question, unsupported language, interpretation timeout) are verbatim duplicates of REQ-003/STORY-003's, already fully implemented by src/question_interpreter.py::interpret_question() and its existing test suite. No new source file or tests were added for STORY-011 specifically — confirmed with the user that reusing the existing implementation outright (rather than writing a second, parallel one) was the correct call, consistent with this repo's reuse-don't-rebuild convention from STORY-006/007. Flagged to the user before closing this out: the brief's own "already specified" list named STORY-009/STORY-010 as prerequisites, but plan.json's real blocked_by is only STORY-001, and STORY-009/010 (releases r3/r4) don't exist in this repo yet.

outstanding: Given a user question, when the system interprets it, then it should suggest at least one potential interpretation.
Given an ambiguous question, when the system interprets it, then it should suggest multiple interpretations for user selection.
Trust: Every interpretation suggestion must be logged with the question and user ID.

criteria.text: Given a user question, when the system analyzes data, then it should provide an accurate answer with an explanation.
Given a complex question, when the system analyzes data, then it should provide an answer with a detailed explanation of the analysis process.
Trust: Every answer provided must be logged with the question, answer, and user ID.

stories.notes: Reuses STORY-003's interpret_question() and STORY-005's explain_results() in full; only new logic is real average/sum/count aggregation and grouping. Caller must specify metric/group_by explicitly (no entity extraction exists), so this computes a pre-specified aggregation rather than truly free-form analysis. comparison/listing intents are cleanly rejected, not computed.

outstanding: Given a user question, when the system analyzes data, then it should provide an accurate answer with an explanation.
Given a complex question, when the system analyzes data, then it should provide an answer with a detailed explanation of the analysis process.
Trust: Every answer provided must be logged with the question, answer, and user ID.

criteria.text: Given a set of data, when I request an executive summary, then the system should provide a concise summary with key KPIs.
Given incomplete data, when I request an executive summary, then the system should indicate missing data and provide available KPIs.
Trust: Every summary request must be logged with the user ID and timestamp.

stories.notes: Reuses STORY-012's analyze_data() (itself built on STORY-003/005) for every KPI's computation and prose, via a synthesized question per KPI spec - no duplicate aggregation math or templates. 'Concise summary' is currently just a one-line success/failure count, not real narrative synthesis across KPIs. Missing data and calculation errors both degrade gracefully per-KPI rather than failing the whole summary.

outstanding: Given a set of data, when I request an executive summary, then the system should provide a concise summary with key KPIs.
Given incomplete data, when I request an executive summary, then the system should indicate missing data and provide available KPIs.
Trust: Every summary request must be logged with the user ID and timestamp.

criteria.text: Given a database, when I inspect schemas, then I should see the structure and relationships of tables.
Given a dataset, when I profile data, then I should see data distribution and quality metrics.
Trust: Every schema inspection and data profiling must be logged with the user ID and timestamp.

stories.notes: schema_inspector.py reuses STORY-001's connect()/execute_query() unmodified (REQ-015 inherited, not reimplemented); tested only against mocked execute_query, never a real SQL Server. data_profiler.py is deliberately self-contained, not reusing csv_upload.py, since that module's public interface takes a file path rather than in-memory rows - confirmed with the user rather than refactoring a file outside this story. Numeric/string dtype split is coarse (no date/datetime detection).

outstanding: Given a database, when I inspect schemas, then I should see the structure and relationships of tables.
